name: Pull to refresh
first: A modifier that lets the user pull a list down to run an async closure that loads its data again, with a spinner until the closure returns.

dependsOn.why: A list on iOS offers the pull, and shows the spinner, when it is given a refresh action.
dependsOn.whyInExample: In an app, `Puller` would be a list, as `list` is on the page of List.

dependsOn.why: The modifier puts the refresh action in the environment, where the list reads it.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The property `@Environment(\.refresh)` reads the action, as `@Environment(\.isEnabled)` reads whether views are enabled.

dependsOn.why: The example calls the refresh action from a task, which can wait for it.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The closure of `task` on line 13 runs in a task, as the one on the page of Task modifier does.

what.is: Pull to refresh lets the user drag a list down to load its data again. The modifier `refreshable` gives it an async closure. Apple's documentation says that a list on iOS then offers the standard pull to refresh: when the user drags the top of the list down, it shows a spinner and runs the closure, and the spinner stays until the closure returns.
what.afterExample: No one pulls here, so `Puller` does what a list does when the user pulls: it reads the refresh action from the environment, and calls it with `await`. Line 15 runs only after `reload()` has returned, which is when a list hides its spinner.
what.problem: Data in a list can change somewhere else, such as trips edited on another device. Users expect to pull a list down to get the newest data, and to see a spinner while it loads. The modifier gives a list that behavior with one closure.
what.how: Apple's documentation says that `refreshable` sets the refresh value in the view's environment to an action that runs the closure, and that views that find the action there, such as a list, offer a way to refresh. The action is async, so the view that calls it waits with `await`, and knows that the refresh is done when the call returns.

when.text: Use it on a list or a scroll view whose data can be loaded again, such as trips kept on a server.
Don't use it for data that only this device changes. That data is always up to date, so there is nothing to load again.

parts.name: The modifier `refreshable`, line 21
parts.text: The modifier puts a refresh action in the environment of `Puller`, and of every view inside it. The action runs the closure after `refreshable`, which calls `reload()`.

parts.name: The refresh action `refresh`, line 10
parts.text: The property `refresh` reads that action from the environment. Where no view put one, it is nil, so line 14 calls it with a question mark, which calls it only when it is there.

steps.text: Lines 20 and 21 make a `Puller` with a refresh action, and line 22 draws it.
Before the `Text` appears, its task starts. Line 14 calls the refresh action, as a list does when the user pulls, and waits.
The action runs the closure on line 21, which calls `reload()`, and line 4 prints {{reloading}}.
Line 5 suspends for 50 milliseconds, while line 23 runs the main run loop. Then line 6 prints {{reloaded}}, and `reload()` returns.
The call on line 14 returns, so line 15 prints {{spinner hides}}, as a list hides its spinner at that moment.

end.text: The view that calls the refresh action waits until the closure has finished, so it knows how long to show the spinner.
